chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) retired to his bed, he would say: 'O Allah, by Your Name I live and by Your Name I die.' And when he rose from his sleep, he would say: 'All praise is for Allah Who gave me life after having caused my death, and to Him is the Resurrection.'

And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever recites at his bedtime the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi) three times, and the Verse in Surah Aal-Imran [Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge], and the Verse of Subservience, and the Verse of Prostration, two devils are assigned to him to protect him from the rebellious devils, whether they will or not, and with them are thirty angels from Allah who praise Allah, glorify Him, declare His oneness, magnify Him, and seek forgiveness for him until that servant awakens from his sleep, and the reward of that is for him.'

key_terms.النُّشُورُ: The Resurrection / The rising from the dead

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and Quranic verses to recite before sleeping in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the prophetic tradition of invoking Allah’s name as the source of life and death, a practice emphasizing total dependence on God (tawakkul) in daily transitions. The detailed benefits of reciting Ayat al-Kursi and other verses underscore the Shia belief in the protective power of Quranic recitation, where specific angels are assigned to guard the sleeper from both minor and major devils, ensuring spiritual safety until awakening.
